observations: A large blue plastic drum with a red lid is shown in three photos.
The drum has a white label with text and a barcode, but the text is not legible.
The drum has a black 'SA' marking on the side, possibly a seller's or inventory mark.
The drum appears to be used, with visible dirt, scuffs, and some water stains on the surface.
The lid is secured with a metal gasket and appears to be intact.
The drum is placed outdoors on a concrete surface, surrounded by other drums and containers.
The seller claims it is a 120-liter plastic drum, but no capacity marking is visible on the drum itself.

claims.evidence: No capacity marking is visible on the drum in any photo. The label is too blurry to read.

claims.claim: Food grade, used only once for clean water. No crack, no leak, lids complete.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The drum may not be food-grade or may have been used for non-food purposes.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the label showing certification marks or a statement of food-grade compliance.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-food-grade or used for non-food purposes

risks.risk: The drum may have cracks, leaks, or structural damage not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the drum's body and lid, showing all seams and joints, and a video of the lid being opened and closed.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially leaking or structurally compromised

risks.risk: The drum may have been previously used for hazardous materials, posing a contamination risk.
risks.proof: A photo of the label showing any hazardous material warnings or a statement of prior use.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the label showing capacity, material, and any certifications.
Close-up photo of the drum's body and lid, showing all seams and joints.
Photo of the label showing any hazardous material warnings or prior use.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
